input.text: s1 (Given): Assume standard integer arithmetic and the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (every integer n >= 2 factors into a finite product of primes).

input.code:
import sympy as sp
a, b = sp.symbols('a b', integer=True)
res = sp.expand((4*a + 1)*(4*b + 1) - (4*(4*a*b + a + b) + 1))
assert res == 0
print('closure identity residual =', res)

input.text: s3 & s4 (Contradiction proof): Suppose there are only finitely many primes p_1, ..., p_k == 3 (mod 4) (k >= 1, with p_1 = 3). Set N = 4*p_1*...*p_k - 1 >= 11. Then N is odd, N == 3 (mod 4), and gcd(N, p_i) = 1 for all i. By the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic, N factors into odd primes (each 1 or 3 mod 4). By induction using the closure identity (4*a + 1)*(4*b + 1) = 4*(4*a*b + a + b) + 1 from s2, a product of primes solely congruent to 1 (mod 4) is congruent to 1 (mod 4), contradicting N == 3 (mod 4). Thus N has a prime factor q == 3 (mod 4) not in {p_1, ..., p_k}, contradiction.

content.text: There are infinitely many prime numbers p congruent to 3 (mod 4).
